issues.section: Prepare for Week 2: check your Geant4 install
issues.quote: Source your Geant4 and ROOT environment and run: geant4-config --version
issues.problem: There are no install instructions for Geant4 11.4 (or its ~2 GB datasets) anywhere: not in the course home, FAQ, primer, Week 1 or README. This is the hardest step for the target audience, and its time is not in any estimate.
issues.fix: Add a 'Week 0 · Set up' item: an official Dockerfile/devcontainer with Geant4 11.4 + datasets + Python stack, a conda-forge route, and a from-source recipe (cmake flags, GEANT4_INSTALL_DATA, expected time and disk). Budget the time.

issues.problem: Week 1 requires ROOT, but the FAQ ('What software do I need?') and README say Weeks 2-8 need only Geant4 + uproot; ROOT is only for musrSim in Week 9.
issues.fix: Drop root-config from the Week 1 check, or say ROOT is optional until Week 9.

issues.quote: Make this layout and paste each file. Open a file to see it.

Macros are shown as one 'macros.txt' with '==== run1.mac ====' separators although the tree lists five files. No zip, no git repo.

issues.section: Hands-on: Labs 8.1 and 8.2 · Create the project from Week 5
issues.quote: Keep Week 5's DetectorConstruction, MuonHit, MuonSD, PrimaryGeneratorAction and ToyScintillatorDigitizer (the generator's commands are now under /week08/gun/).
issues.problem: Week 5's PrimaryGeneratorAction registers /week05/gun/. A student who keeps it as told runs daq.mac, whose '/week08/gun/model cos2' is then an unknown command. As Week 2's UIMAN box warns, the rest of the batch macro is skipped.
issues.fix: Make it an explicit edit: 'In PrimaryGeneratorAction.cc change "/week05/gun/" to "/week08/gun/"', or show the file.

issues.quote: popt, pcov = curve_fit(osc, tg, A, p0=[0.25, 1.35, 0.0, 0.05], ...)
issues.problem: asymmetry.py seeds every fit at the 10 mT frequency. In my run of run_scan.sh the 20 mT fit locked onto the wrong minimum: f = 1.3528 ± 0.0289 MHz, chi2/ndf 1859.9/176, A0 WARNING. field_scan.py ignores the warning and reports pull −46.99, slope 135.372 ± 0.068, chi2/ndf 2203/3. The same data with p0 f=2.71 gives the page's 2.7069 MHz. The page's success depends on the thread race it mentions.
issues.fix: Pass the expected frequency (from the file name or --f0) or seed from a periodogram/FFT; make field_scan.py fail loudly if asymmetry.py prints WARNING or chi2/ndf > 2.

issues.section: Check the integrator before blaming the physics
issues.quote: The 1 GeV σ differs from step 3 (0.0031 against 0.0040) because the run produces different random scattering, not because of integration: compare in units of its own error.
issues.problem: The lab intro promises '±3% relative on σ'; this is a 25% change. reconstruct.py uses np.std, which a few scattering outliers dominate. Bootstrap of the 1 GeV sample gives σ = 0.0040 ± 0.00046 (±11%), with the largest |Δp/p| = 5.4%. The robust half-width is 0.0029. No error is printed, so 'units of its own error' cannot be applied.
issues.fix: Use the central-68% half-width (as the toy does), print a bootstrap error next to σ, and correct the ±3% claim.

issues.section: Run 200 000 muons and check the field first
issues.quote: G4cout << "Field at (0,0,0): Bx = " << fB / tesla * 1000. << " mT  (printFieldValueAtPoint analogue)"
issues.problem: This prints the configured member variable, not the field the transport uses. It cannot catch a wrong axis, scale or offset, which is exactly what section 10.1 ('A field can be wrong while the simulation runs perfectly') tells students to check.
issues.fix: Call field->GetFieldValue(point, B) at (0,0,0) and a few off-centre points and print all three components.

issues.quote: secondaries per event, by particle:   e- 2.387   gamma 1.358
issues.problem: RunAction prints one species per line. With 'grep -A4 "=== Census"' the student sees a 'CPU time per event' line and only e-, never gamma. The Run B expected output ('by particle:' / 'by creator :') is also a reformatted summary, not literal output. The numbers match exactly.
issues.fix: Paste literal output, or label it 'summarised'; use grep -A8.

issues.quote: if (list == "EM") ... else runManager->SetUserInitialization(new FTFP_BERT());
issues.problem: Any first argument other than 'EM' (typo 'em', or 'QGSP_BIC') silently runs FTFP_BERT. That is exactly the kind of silent physics choice the page's 'Four ways a physics choice fails without a sound' warns about.
issues.fix: Reject unknown names with a usage message, or use G4PhysListFactory and print the list actually built.

issues.quote: Usage: ./week03 run100.mac > concrete.log && python3 steps_summary.py concrete.log
issues.problem: There is no run100.mac (only run1.mac and run1000.mac). steps_summary.py is also the only analysis script that CMake does not copy into build/; weeks 4, 5, 7, 8 and 10 copy theirs.
issues.fix: Fix the docstring to run1000.mac and add steps_summary.py to the configure_file loop.

issues.quote: Each muon also zig-zags slightly as it passes many nuclei (multiple Coulomb scattering, Week 4).
issues.problem: Week 4 does not cover multiple scattering. The first real use is Week 7's 'scattering term' of σp/p, which appears only inside the toy's approximations box (Highland formula). A non-physicist cannot see why that term is flat in p.
issues.fix: Add a short Definition (Highland θ0 ∝ √(x/X0)/p) to Week 7 section 7.1 and fix the primer's cross-reference.

issues.section: FAQ · What software do I need?
issues.quote: Weeks 2–8, 10 and 11 need Geant4 11.4 ... and Python with numpy, scipy, matplotlib, uproot and awkward.
issues.problem: There are no pinned versions (no requirements.txt or environment.yml), no CI, and no Dockerfile in the repository. Reproducibility is a course theme (Week 12), but the course itself has no reproducible environment.
issues.fix: Add requirements.txt (Week 1 already names NumPy 2.5.3), environment.yml, a Dockerfile, and a CI job that builds code/weekNN and compares key lines with the pages.

issues.quote: code/week02/pion_tracks.json, code/week05/run_c_both_above.json, code/week01/__pycache__/
issues.problem: Site-generation data and Python bytecode sit next to student code. A student who downloads code/ gets files the page never mentions.
issues.fix: Move page data to tools/ or assets/data and add a .gitignore.

issues.section: Build and read the overlap check
issues.quote: ./week03 run1.mac | grep -i overlap
issues.problem: The 'expected' block for the broken case shows the full G4Exception banner, but grep only prints the 4 lines containing 'overlap'.
issues.fix: Use grep -i -A6 GeomVol1002, or say the banner is shown in full for reference.

issues.section: Version everything / Let a stranger reproduce the headline (repro_check.sh)
issues.quote: EXE=$(find . -maxdepth 1 -type f -perm -u+x ! -name '*.sh' | head -1)
issues.problem: Guessing the executable picks the wrong file if a .py ends up executable. The 'tree not clean' test runs right after a fresh clone, so it can never fail.
issues.fix: Take the executable name as an argument and drop or relocate the clean-tree check.

issues.section: Fill the proposal and get it signed off
issues.quote: Fill the proposal and get it signed off
issues.problem: For a self-paced paying student it is not stated who signs off the proposal, who the 'partner' or referee is, or who grades with the Definition 12.2 weights.
issues.fix: State the mechanism per tier (self-assessment rubric vs TA review).

issues.quote: the trigger needs both counters within a 15 ns window
issues.problem: The event display uses 15 ns; the lesson, code and quiz use 20 ns.
issues.fix: Use 20 ns everywhere.

issues.quote: Signal s; ... [](const std::map<std::string, G4int>& m)
issues.problem: Local variables named s and m shadow Geant4's unit constants second and metre (-Wshadow). It is harmless here but a classic Geant4 trap worth avoiding in teaching code.
issues.fix: Rename to sig and counts, and mention the trap in a common-errors box.
